person: Joel Martinez is a 38-year-old warehouse shift supervisor who does the family's bills on his laptop on Sunday nights. His mother-in-law, Rosa Delgado, 79, was admitted to Saint Ardent as an inpatient on 8 September, switched to observation the next day, and sent to Oakview Care on 12 September. Oakview has billed the rehab privately, $7,850, because Medicare says she had no qualifying stay. Joel has a power of representation on file for her through his wife, but it is his wife's mother and he is the one reading the paperwork. He is fair and frustrated, wants to pay only what is really owed, and has already paid one bill twice this year, so he does not want anything paid or sent without being asked.
stated_up_front: My mother-in-law's rehab at Oakview got billed to us because the hospital switched her to 'observation' after they admitted her in September. Can you look at it and tell me what we actually owe and whether there's anything we can do about it before I pay anything?

facts.about: Which hospital stay is the problem
facts.truth: September: admitted as an inpatient on 8 September, changed to observation on 9 September, discharged to Oakview on 12 September.
A statement of $7,850 for her rehab days starting 12 September, because Medicare did not count the hospital stay as qualifying.

facts.about: Hospital balance on the September stay
facts.truth: Saint Ardent billing shows a balance of $1,486 that Joel has not paid.

facts.about: A different stay that was observation from the start
facts.truth: In April she had three nights in a regular room, but the ER put her on observation from the beginning and there was never an inpatient order.

facts.about: An older stay from last year
facts.truth: In October 2024 she had a stay that was changed to observation the same way, and nobody appealed it at the time.

facts.about: A stay that already worked fine
facts.truth: In July she was an inpatient for four days and Oakview's rehab after it was covered by Medicare and paid.
Rosa signed a paper in the hospital about the change to observation, and nobody told the family they could appeal it.

facts.about: Whether an appeal has been filed
facts.truth: Joel believes nobody has filed any appeal for the September stay.

facts.about: Who is contacting him about help
facts.truth: A company mailed and left messages offering to fight the bill for a share of what Medicare pays back, which Joel has ignored so far.
Joel's wife, Rosa's daughter, is the appointed representative on Medicare.gov, and Joel uses her login with her okay.

unknowns: Whether the hospital's switch from inpatient to observation was actually allowed or handled correctly
How many days Medicare counts as inpatient for the September stay
Whether the October 2024 stay can still be appealed
What the Condition Code 44 on the hospital paperwork means
Whether Oakview will pause the bill while an appeal is pending
